report.narrative:
This bot buys into rising price trends and adds to losing positions, exposing capital to severe market reversals. Across 300 closed trades, that trend-following approach achieved a win rate of 93.3%. The profit factor on closed trades is 41.52, meaning gains vastly exceeded losses on positions the bot actually finished. However, the strategy shows signs of holding losers, currently carrying an unrealised loss of 0.9% on open positions. Marking those open positions to market reduces the profit factor to 13.5. The Sharpe ratio reaches 27.2, reflecting smooth returns relative to variability because unprofitable trades stayed open. Simulations across 10,000 scenarios show a 0% probability of ruin, but the simulation sees closed trades only without that open loss. The risk score of 42.4 reflects that real probability of losing capital.

Performance data shows heavy reliance on rising markets, where volatile uptrends generated 49% of total profit using 18x leverage. Calm uptrends contributed 21% of total profit at 19.8x leverage, further demonstrating that upward bias. The bot has never traded through an extended downtrend, leaving its long-biased stacking behaviour untested in market drops. Closed trades recorded a max drawdown of 0.2%, describing the deepest equity dip experienced during those favourable historical rallies. A longest losing streak of 4 closed trades helped keep recorded dips shallow. That smooth closed history masks the danger of adding to losing trades when crypto trends turn downward.

report.verdict_basis: Method: 10,000 scenarios simulated with a stationary bootstrap (Politis and Romano, 1994) on the closed trades of the bot itself — this preserves the autocorrelation of the sequence and assumes no normal distribution. Tail risk is measured with VaR at the 95% level and CVaR (expected shortfall). Sharpe quality is measured with the Probabilistic Sharpe Ratio and the Deflated Sharpe Ratio (Bailey and López de Prado, 2012 and 2014) — which strip out the edge that appears by luck alone when many candidates are screened — together with the Minimum Track Record Length, which states how many trades are needed before a Sharpe ratio means anything. Out-of-sample validation on 36 bots: the Spearman rank correlation between the risk score and later drawdown is 0.64 (95% confidence interval [0.39–0.80]). This score does NOT predict profit or loss — the confidence interval for its correlation with return contains zero.
